methodology.purpose: Measure security-semantic parity against source-supported effective authority rather than raw lexical entity counts.
methodology.review_method: Policy-aligned LLM source review followed by source verification and explicit observed/inferred/unresolved evidence states.
methodology.scanner_change_policy: No scanner change is part of this benchmark commit. The benchmark is a separate post-hoc semantic layer and does not rewrite frozen ground truth.

agent_principals.note: Seven constructors are in api/tools.py and four additional constructors are in connected repository modules.

effective_tools.note: The locked reference's 17 tool assertions include repeated agent-to-tool bindings; they are not 17 unique implementations.

mcp_servers.note: Six McpToolset construction sites bind the same in-repository DuckDB stdio implementation with construction-specific authority.

authority_facts.fact: Agent constructors repeatedly bind skillset and duckdb_mcp instances; bindings must retain source-instance provenance rather than collapse by variable name.
Reviewed agent-side DuckDB MCP constructors pass read_only=True.

regression_assertions.reason: Cross-file ADK closure should recover all observed agent constructors.
Distinct MCP construction instances must not be collapsed before authority binding.

cases.known_current_gap: Cross-file closure and construction-instance identity for repeated ADK tool/MCP bindings.

agent_principals.note: AgentLoop is a bounded LLM tool-calling execution loop even though the locked lexical reference contains no agent root.

effective_tools.note: Custom @tool metadata is recursively auto-discovered into ToolRegistry and exposed through OpenAI-compatible tool definitions.

mcp_servers.note: MCPClient can manage multiple configured stdio servers and dynamically register their tools.

authority_facts.fact: ToolRegistry.get_tool_definitions supplies tool schemas to the model and ToolRegistry.execute dispatches selected calls.
Effective authority is filtered by allowed_tools, runtime gates, operator-only controls, subagent exclusions, dynamic MCP availability and remote connector availability.
Subagents instantiate AgentLoop dynamically and remove unsafe tools including create_tool, reload_tools, spawn_subagent and wait_for_subagent.
http_request can resolve $CRED{name} through the vault before outbound HTTP; implementation also contains SSRF, redirect, authorization-stripping and response-bounding mitigations.

regression_assertions.reason: Framework-neutral model/tool loops should be represented as agents when model selection and dispatch are source-proven.
Custom registry/decorator tools should be discoverable without framework-specific decorators.

cases.known_current_gap: Framework-neutral model/tool-loop and generic tool-registry discovery with conditional authority.

agent_principals.note: The active default registry loads six config-defined agents; additional directly constructed agents exist elsewhere in the repository.

authority_facts.fact: User query reaches WorkflowRouterAgent; model output can select call_tool or call_agent and OrchestrationEngine executes the selected action.
WorkflowRouterAgent has get_agent_memory, update_agent_memory and add_to_agent_memory_list authority from active configuration.
MemoryStore persists memory under data/memory and update operations can target an agent_name supplied through tool parameters.

required.reason: State-changing persistent-memory tools lack an explicit approval boundary.
Privileged data-write memory tools lack a detected guardrail or approval.
Router/data-gathering authority combines memory read and write capabilities.
Untrusted user input reaches model-directed persistent memory writes.

candidate.reason: Memory update target agent_name is dynamically supplied and no static caller-only scope was found.

cases.known_current_gap: Config-driven registry resolution and custom orchestration do not propagate tool authority and input trust into policy evaluation.

mcp_servers.note: The first FastMCP assignment is overwritten; only the replacement object is used by mcp.run().

authority_facts.fact: CLI user input is passed to the Pydantic AI agent with the MCP server bound.
The effective MCP exposes state-changing operations including save_figure, clear_figure and close_figure without an explicit approval/guardrail boundary.

required.reason: The effective MCP exposes privileged state-changing tools without explicit action boundary.
Untrusted CLI input can drive model-selected MCP calls to destructive/state-clearing operations.

regression_assertions.reason: Overwritten FastMCP construction must not survive as an effective runtime server.
One effective server must not create duplicate identical findings.

cases.known_current_gap: Object lifetime/reassignment creates duplicate MCP entities/findings and trust does not propagate from CLI input to MCP destructive authority.

agent_principals.note: One compiled LangGraph agent architecture is instantiated by multiple application surfaces; workflow nodes are not separate security principals.

effective_tools.note: Locked reference tool assertions contain lexical/decorator duplicates.

mcp_servers.note: The local time MCP is a stdio server; a commented remote fetch server is not live authority.

authority_facts.fact: FastAPI ChatRequest.query becomes HumanMessage content and reaches the LangGraph tool-capable agent.
execute_sqlite_query calls sqlite cursor.execute(query) and commits every non-SELECT query; it does not spawn a process.
The safer mutation filter in main.py is not the implementation bound as execute_sqlite_query in the LangGraph tools list.

required.reason: Model-controlled SQL can include destructive operations and is committed without approval.
The bound SQL tool can perform state-changing INSERT/UPDATE and other writes without approval.
Privileged DB mutation lacks an explicit guardrail/approval boundary.
The agent combines database read and write authority.
Untrusted HTTP user input reaches a model-selected tool capable of destructive SQLite statements.

forbidden.reason: sqlite3 cursor.execute is SQL execution, not shell/process execution.

cases.known_current_gap: SQL execution is misclassified as process execution and input trust is not carried to destructive database authority.

effective_tools.note: The in-repository MCP server exposes numerous project, character, pattern, narrative, symbolic, plotline and FastAgent tools; exhaustive semantic tool count was not locked in this adjudication.

mcp_servers.note: Initialization generates four named stdio aliases that all launch mcp_server/server.py; runtime availability remains conditional on the optional FastAgent dependency.

authority_facts.fact: FastAgent agents are declared with @fast.agent decorators and explicit servers=[...] bindings.
writing_workflow is a five-stage @fast.chain and story_refinement is an @fast.evaluator_optimizer workflow.
When FastAgent is installed and initialization runs, named MCP aliases launch the same in-repository MCP server implementation.

candidate.reason: Conditionally bound in-repository MCP aliases expose state-changing project tools without an explicit action boundary.
Some FastAgent server bindings combine project read and state-changing authority when the generated MCP configuration is active.

regression_assertions.reason: All eight decorated FastAgent principals should be structurally visible when the optional integration source is present.

cases.known_current_gap: FastAgent decorators/workflows and generated MCP server bindings are structurally invisible; conditional runtime authority must be retained as conditional rather than asserted as unconditional.

agent_principals.note: Multiple Agent() lexical occurrences include examples/docstrings and instantiation sites; they are not four independent principals.

authority_facts.fact: OAuthClientProvider implements authorization-code/refresh-token authentication and is passed to HTTP/SSE MCP transports.
session.list_tools returns the remote MCP catalogue and all returned tools are passed to the LLM without an explicit allowlist.
CLI --url or Agent.add_mcp accepts the remote MCP destination; no destination allowlist was found.
The documented/default Notion configuration uses https://mcp.notion.com/mcp.

required.reason: All remote list_tools results are exposed to the model without an explicit tool allowlist.
Remote MCP destination is caller-selected and lacks a detected destination restriction.

forbidden.reason: Recognized OAuth authentication is explicitly configured.
The observed documented/default Notion endpoint is HTTPS; a dynamic URL alone does not prove plaintext transport.

cases.known_current_gap: Custom remote-MCP model/tool loop is visible only superficially; authentication is not converted into policy semantics and dynamic tool/destination scope is not evaluated.
